questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Location: I always wanted to live in NYC. University: New York University is a prestige university, hereby positioning myself better in my future career, where I hope to work international to some extent.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I arrived half a month before study start. Which I consider to have been a huge advantage. It was nice to have time exploring the city and getting to know the different NYU buildings. In that way I also had time to meet with people at the Student Link Center, who could inform me on practical matters.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: NYU has an amazing exchange staff, that assists in everything from VISA-application to social events. And they basically informed, and guided me the whole way. Upon arrival I went to the Student Link center to get my NYU card, there I also went later in the month to meet the other exchange students. That meeting was facilitated by the exchange staff at NYU.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty difficult to find off campus housing, and the prices are very high. However, I managed, through a friend of mine, to rent a room in his apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be ready to pay minimum 1300 USD pr. month.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am only unsatisfied with the housing, because of the price.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registered through the exchange system at the University of Copenhagen. It was fairly easy, and people in the exchange team at KU, was very helpful and easy to contact.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Guidance in terms of mailing. Information meetings and an overall introduction lecture to exchange abroad.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull, I got all the classes I wanted at NYU.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register as fast as possible!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took all undergraduate courses, and they were fairly manageable. I had no problems keeping up with the level at all!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The students pr. lecture and class were less, meaning that you got to know the professor better. It was a nice format, where you got more personal with everyone involved: student as well as professor and TA

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Human Rights and Culture, 
Climate and Society, 
Language, Power and Identity.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Climate and Society - It was super exciting to enter environmental studies, and I learned a lot.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Crazy housing prices, and also the food: it is very expensive!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was more expensive than I expected. I did not encounter any "less expensive" items.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports activities, social events, gym and swimming hall, lectures etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did a lot outside the University, hanging out with other danish people who were interns at the UN or the danish embassy. But I would recommend joining the Yoga sessions, as well as using the gym.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go Upstate for hiking! Take the boat to Queens and New Jersey. And go rooftop partying.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. It is a very international environment which is reflected in a diversity of cultures - made it easy to navigate.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: People are very open, so I think you will have no problems with that.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was an extreme consumer behaviour, which I personally found a bit frustrating.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness and openness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Relax, Take a student loan and go have the best half year! It is worth every penny!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of poverty in New York, and you should therefore always be mindfull what areas you go to.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new amazing people and living in New York.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The high prices.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
